item.title: SCP-3219:
item.content:encoded: There's something going on that means Ashley and any other possible survivors had to stay up high. Storm cellar, blocking pipes, holing up in the attic - all to get further away from ground level and whatever is down there. Safe bet they get dragged under the earth (hence the psychic quilt of taphophobia) and kept alive for a little while? That explains the all the nasty in the water samples. This is that good good spooky and I am HERE for it. Upvoted!

item.title: SCP 5129 - Literal Thinking Glasses: Glasses for Improvement :)
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I can see that you have a somewhat smooth flow of writing in your article, and has a quite concrete view of what you want to convey to the reader. This is already a good sign that you are developing your potential, but as of the moment, I think that you should be more attuned into how people should write SCPs, particularly in terms of clinical tone and the uniqueness of your idea.

Speaking of uniqueness, you can do it by expounding on a single idea from your SCP. For example, you mentioned that it is "8-bit" - why? What is the story behind it? You can do a social commentary on how gamers (hardcore, casual, anything) perceive each other, or reality in general, for example, just by basing off that "8-bit" detail.

You can also tell the story of the Crypt Night Club - it does sound like a good GoI after all. Why are they connected with your 8-bit glasses? There's potential here, and I am somewhat interested in it.

In short, you should focus on polishing your clinical tone, your idea (once again, focus on one thing), and have a good story or narrative in mind. "Perception defines reality" - how can this be uniquely written considering that you have things like "8-bit" and the night club?

Good luck, and have a good time writing again for this site :)

item.title: SCP-3195: 1+
item.content:encoded:
I honestly really enjoyed this one, although i don't personally have relationship problems with my mother this made me feel bad for the SCP and the interviewer despite me having to experience what they have went (or still going) through, so props to you.

As said above the casual interview logs are a bit of a problem for some people. For me they un-immerse me a little but this in my opinion made me see both the characters as just, well guys with mother issues, not some soulless interviewer and some SCP.

Also the death at the end seemed really out of place to me, like i was just thinking "Dam did it really just die?". Also if it is dead then why is its classification Euclid and not Neutralized?

All and all a pretty good SCP, hope this helps :P

item.title: Operation Galahad:
item.content:encoded:
I like this - an article devoted to pure collaborative worldbuilding, while controversial, is something I personally find interesting. But, as an avid world builder, I have some criticism to give.

+ Show
- hide

The Chitin Sea
Source of the River Tock… Immeasurably large biomass

This breaks one of the most important rules of worldbuilding 'rivers don't flow upwards.' As it is never specified that the river tock flows in reverse, or that the Chitan is built on higher ground than the rest of corbenic, so I'm gonna say that this river doesn't really make sense. It would probably be better to change this to something like:

The Chitin Sea
Found by following the Right Moon from the Great Desert, Valley of the Striders or following the River Tock to its mouth. Immeasurably large biomass…

Furthermore:

which is above the cloud layer and has not yet been observed, is said to contain the castle of SCP-PC-007

Is this cloud layer constant? If so, that should probably be specified.

Otherwise, I would love to see more of the culture of Corbenics inhabitants. At the moment we have some information on the structure of corbenic, but I'd love to see how the citizens of corbenic act, maybe in the form of 'essays' (maybe similar to those in SCP-4935 and SCP-5005) by project Galahad members based on testimonies from the Omega-16 group. But that's just my opinion. +1 anyway.
